Upstream documentation alignment

Source: vignettes/upstream-alignment.Rmd
upstream-alignment.Rmd

Purpose

This ledger records how shinyAssistantUI evaluates the assistant-ui documentation in official order. A page moves from Pending only after its concepts have been checked against the current R, JavaScript, and Shiny architecture. Each record must identify current source evidence and classify missing one-to-one upstream behavior as covered, an architectural choice, not applicable, or a real gap. Later pages are not treated as adopted merely because a related feature already exists.

Ordered review status

Order Official page Status Local landing point Conclusion
1 Documentation Adopted Homepage + Overview React Web + custom ExternalStoreRuntime + Shiny transport
2 Installation Adapted Installation R package + bundled web assets + optional R backends; no end-user npm
3 Agent Skills Pending — Next official page; not yet investigated

The first two pages have been reviewed in official order. A later page advances only after its own upstream and local-source audit.

Record 1 — Documentation

Reviewed: 2026-09-07

Upstream page: assistant-ui Documentation

Result: Adopted; documentation clarification only, with no product-code change.

The upstream landing page is a map of assistant-ui rather than a single installation recipe. Its Quickstart, surface choices, runtime choices, and links to deeper guides establish four decisions for this package:

Upstream area shinyAssistantUI interpretation Decision
Quickstart Start with a minimal Shiny app and an R handler Document in the Overview
Surface choices Use the existing React Web surface inside an htmlwidget Keep; React Native and Ink are out of scope
Runtime choices Use the package’s custom ExternalStoreRuntime and R server bridge Keep; “your own server” is the closest upstream model
Quick links Route users to Overview, articles, reference, and changelog Represent in pkgdown navigation

Architecture alignment 

assistant-ui React Web
  + custom ExternalStoreRuntime
  + Shiny R <-> JavaScript transport
  + backend-agnostic R handler

This combination is intentional. The custom runtime is the adapter between assistant-ui’s React state and Shiny’s event channel; it does not require a hosted assistant-ui backend. ClaudeAgentSDK, ellmer, and custom handlers are integration choices above that bridge.

Explicit non-requirements

The first page does not create a requirement to support every surface or install every listed adapter. For shinyAssistantUI:

  • React Native and Ink do not match the package’s browser-based Shiny surface.
  • AG-UI, A2A, A2UI, and other runtime adapters are not installed by this work.
  • The existing Shiny transport and ExternalStoreRuntime are not replaced.
  • No Installation article is authored before the second official page is reviewed.

Local evidence

The mapping is represented in three durable places:

  1. The pkgdown homepage states the package’s React Web, Shiny, and backend-agnostic position.
  2. The Overview provides a minimal app and concept mapping.
  3. The reference index groups all current documented package topics by user task.

Record 2 — Installation

Reviewed: 2026-09-07

Upstream page: assistant-ui Installation

Result: Adapted to the R package boundary; documentation changes only.

The upstream page assumes a React application assembled with the assistant-ui CLI or shadcn, npm packages, a JavaScript AI SDK endpoint, environment credentials, and an explicit React runtime provider. The current shinyAssistantUI package was checked rather than treating those assumptions as universal requirements.

Source coverage

Installation concern Local source evidence Finding
Browser bundle R/assistantUI.R resolves JS/CSS/KaTeX from installed inst/www Users already receive the compiled surface
Runtime wiring assistantUIOutput() and assistantUIServer() connect Shiny to ExternalStoreRuntime No React provider code required in the app
Backend endpoint assistantUIServer() invokes a callback contract R handler replaces the Next.js API route
Optional providers DESCRIPTION Suggests plus Claude, ellmer, and codeagent handler factories Install only the selected backend
Thread navigation and modal show_thread_list and modal server/output options Existing source features, now exposed in installation docs
Contributor rebuild package.json, lockfile, Vite build, then R installation Node/npm belong to source development only

Omission classification

Difference from upstream Classification Reason
No assistant-ui CLI or shadcn command for users Architecture choice The component tree is maintained and compiled inside the R package
No JavaScript AI SDK provider matrix Ecosystem adaptation R integrations use ellmer, ClaudeAgentSDK, codeagent, or the generic handler contract
No single required API key Architecture choice Credentials are owned by the selected backend; a custom handler may need none
No CRAN/stable package-manager route Real distribution gap The current public route is the GitHub development repository
No declared minimum supported R version Real metadata/test gap No compatibility matrix supports a truthful version promise yet
Remote codeagent cannot receive live host-defined tools Real implementation limitation Live ellmer chat objects are not serializable across the worker boundary

The audit found no missing installation step needed to make the existing core surface load from an installed package. It did find documentation omissions—the bundled asset boundary, optional backend prerequisites, existing thread-list/modal entry points, and contributor-only Node workflow—which are now covered by the Installation guide. The three real gaps remain explicit; this review does not claim to implement them.

Next review boundary

Agent Skills is now the next official page and remains Pending. Its upstream behavior and the current load_claude_skills()/connected-CLI paths must be investigated in a separate source audit before its status changes.
